An independent day school for boys and girls aged 11-18 on the bank of the River Thames in Sonning, Berkshire.
We exist to inspire in every student a lifelong love of learning and the confidence to flourish. At Reading Blue Coat, we equip young people to thrive in a rapidly changing world while nurturing a happy, kind and inclusive community where students feel valued and supported. Through this, we develop grounded, outward‑looking young people ready to lead fulfilling lives and make a positive contribution to the world.

Inspiring intellectual curiosity and academic ambition.
Our academic life is defined by ambitious standards and exceptional teaching. We encourage intellectual curiosity and independent thought, helping students achieve strong outcomes while building self-belief and adaptability for life beyond school.
Our values guide everything we do, building character and shaping individuals who contribute positively to society.
Aspiration
In every area of our lives, to seek to do our best, making the most of our talents and the opportunities we have.
Compassion
To be aware of the needs of others and respond with care, individually and collectively, to those around us.
Courage
To meet, rather than avoid, the challenges and difficulties we face, supported and encouraged by others.
Integrity
Even where there is a potential personal cost, to always seek to do the right thing.
Service
To serve others as members of communities, strengthening them for the benefit of all.
Discovering and nurturing passions through challenge and exploration.
Adventure Education
We believe young people learn as much beyond the classroom as they do within it, gaining resilience and independence through discovery and outdoor experiences.
Sport
Sport is about far more than physical fitness. It teaches teamwork, perseverance and respect, helping students develop qualities that last a lifetime.
Performing Arts
Creative expression transforms learning. Through drama, music and dance, students learn to communicate ideas and connect with others in meaningful ways.
Clubs and Societies
Our rich programme of clubs and societies encourages individuality and originality, offering opportunities to explore interests, share ideas and form lasting friendships.

Through service to others, students broaden their perspective and strengthen their commitment to making a difference in our communities.

Performing Arts
In the Performing Arts, students are encouraged to take creative risks, work with passion and discipline, and express themselves with confidence, all within a supportive and dynamic community.
At Reading Blue Coat, the Performing Arts are far more than a co-curricular offering – they are a vital part of how students learn, grow and connect with the world around them.
The purpose of all art is, ultimately, to explore the meaning and purpose of existence. In the Performing Arts, we discover new ways of seeing – new ways of understanding ourselves, others and our place in the wider world. Artistic expression demands more than talent: it calls for imagination, courage, discipline and openness. It invites students to let go of preconceptions, embrace creativity and allow space for transformation – of ideas, of perspective and often, of self.
Students engage with a broad range of artistic disciplines including Dance, Drama, Music, Public Speaking and Technical Theatre, as well as the visual arts such as painting and sculpture. Across all these fields, their achievements are frequently outstanding and recognised at local, national and international levels.
Our vibrant calendar of concerts, recitals, productions, exhibitions and debates is a highlight of school life. These events are not only a celebration of student talent, but also of community spirit, and we are always delighted to welcome parents, friends and alumni to support and share in these moments.
Whether on stage, behind the scenes or at the podium, every student is given the chance to find their voice and pursue excellence. With opportunities to perform in professional-standard productions, compete on international stages or simply explore the joy of creative expression, the Performing Arts are a vibrant and integral part of life at Reading Blue Coat.
Drama
The Drama Department at Reading Blue Coat is a vibrant and dynamic space where stories are brought to life. Through performance, design and critical exploration, students are encouraged to think creatively, collaborate with others, and develop their voice. Whether working on a script, devising original work or taking to the stage, students build confidence, empathy, and a deeper understanding of the world around them.
Dance
The Dance Department at Reading Blue Coat is an energetic and expressive environment where students develop technique, strength, and artistry. Through a range of styles and performance opportunities, students are challenged to push their physical boundaries while exploring creativity through movement. Dance at RBC fosters discipline, resilience and a strong sense of ensemble, empowering students to perform with confidence and individuality.
Curricular Drama
All students in Year 7 enjoy dedicated Drama lessons, where they are introduced to key theatrical terminology and the foundations of theatre history. In Years 8 & 9, students can choose Drama, allowing them to further develop their skills through the exploration of a range of genres and texts, alongside practical experience in elements such as lighting and sound design.
At GCSE and A Level, students follow the Eduqas specification. Students can specialise in acting or technical/design pathways, developing their understanding of influential practitioners such as Augusto Boal, Bertolt Brecht and Konstantin Stanislavski. Through both scripted and devised work, they grow as performers, directors, designers, and thoughtful critics.
Learning is enriched through a wide range of opportunities beyond the classroom. Theatre Maker Days provide students with the chance to experience professional performance in a variety of settings – from West End productions to more intimate venues such as The Mill at Sonning – broadening their understanding of style, genre, and theatrical practice.
Curricular Dance
Dance was introduced into the curriculum in September 2023 under the leadership of our Head of Dance, marking an exciting and ambitious development in the Performing Arts provision at Reading Blue Coat.
The Dance curriculum is designed to develop students’ technical ability, physical confidence, and creative expression. From the outset, all students in Year 7 have Dance lessons and students are encouraged to explore a range of styles and techniques, building strength, coordination, and performance quality. Alongside this, they begin to develop their choreographic voice, learning how to create and communicate meaning through movement.
As the subject continues to grow, students will have the opportunity to pursue Dance at GCSE and A Level. At GCSE, students develop their skills as both performers and choreographers, studying set works and analysing professional repertoire alongside practical performance and composition. At A Level, this is extended further, with a deeper focus on technical excellence, choreographic intention and critical appreciation of key practitioners and dance styles.
Across all key stages, students are encouraged to think creatively, work collaboratively, and refine their physical and expressive skills. The curriculum fosters discipline, resilience, and artistry, supporting students to grow not only as dancers, but as confident and reflective performers.
Learning is enhanced through performance opportunities and exposure to live and recorded professional work, enabling students to engage with dance as both an art form and a means of communication.
Co-Curricular Drama
Performance is at the heart of the Drama co-curricular programme, with a variety of productions staged throughout the year:
Students are encouraged to take on a variety of roles, from acting and directing to technical and design work, helping them develop confidence, creativity, and collaboration skills.
Co-Curricular Dance
Dance is a dynamic and vibrant part of our co-curricular programme. Students can take part in a wide range of classes and styles, including contemporary, street, commercial, ballet and jazz.
The annual Dance Show is a highlight of the year, showcasing the creativity, athleticism, and dedication of our dancers. Blue Coat also competes in inter-school competitions, giving students the opportunity to perform at a high-level while being part of a supportive and exciting performance community.
Through both performance and competition, students develop technique, artistry, and confidence, while enjoying the collaborative and expressive nature of dance.
Technical Theatre
Every production is supported by a student technical crew, who gain hands-on experience in lighting, sound and set design under the expert guidance of our Theatre Technical Director. We maintain the highest standards in health and safety across our performance spaces.
For those wanting to get involved with technology in the arts, the School Media Team meet as a weekly Technical Theatre club.
Music
The aim of the Music Department is to provide a wealth of opportunities for all students to make and enjoy music. Whether it’s singing in choirs, composing film soundtracks, listening to music from a range of cultures or recording songs in our studio, music at RBC is for everyone.
Music is taught both as an academic subject and through an extensive co-curricular programme. In the classroom, students are encouraged to explore composition, performance and music appreciation. Beyond lessons, we offer a vibrant array of ensembles including our Jazz Band, Rock Bands, String Orchestra, Choirs and smaller wind and brass groups. Theory and composition clubs further extend our provision.
Curricular Music
Music lessons are designed to develop the interconnected skills of listening, performing, composing and appraising. Studying music enables students to become creative thinkers, analytical problem solvers, and effective communicators.
Throughout Key Stage 3 Music, students:
• Build core listening, composing and performing skills. • Acquire musical vocabulary and develop the necessary skills to apply it effectively. • Develop their ability to describe and evaluate music, forming views and expressing and justifying personal opinions. • Strengthen their musical ear and notational awareness. • Understand different musical traditions and the role music plays in both our national identity and global culture, as well as in personal identity. • Explore how ideas, experiences and emotions are conveyed in music from different times and cultures. • Understand the potential of music technology and develop skills in using it to create their own music.
GCSE Music is a popular subject in which students can develop their own musical interests as well as their skills. Students have achieved excellent results, and we follow the OCR specification.
A Level Music is ideal for passionate musicians who want to delve into musical analysis and compose and perform at a high level. Results have been superb, and many students go on to study music at university or conservatoire.
Co-Curricular Music
Whether students take individual lessons or not, there is a broad co-curricular programme. The programme includes:
• Symphony Orchestra (for all instrumentalists) • Big Band (for advanced players) • Bash Cats (the junior jazz band) • Chamber Choir (by audition) • Treble Choir (for Years 7 and 8) • Senior String Ensemble (for advanced players) • Rock bands, alongside several smaller wind and brass groups • Theory and composition sessions
All students in Year 7 are auditioned and invited to join ensembles. However, students are welcome and encouraged to join at any point in their musical journey.
We aim to provide a wide range of performance opportunities for students at all stages of their development. Large formal concerts, showcasing ensembles and soloists, are a wonderful celebration. Equally, smaller informal recitals provide valuable opportunities for students to build confidence.
Individual Music Lessons, LAMDA & Trinity Musical Theatre
Students at Reading Blue Coat have the opportunity to develop their musical and performance skills through a range of individual tuition and graded performance programmes.
Inspiring Events
Across the academic year, our young musicians – supported by a talented team of staff – take part in an inspiring calendar of events, including the Grand Concert, chamber concerts and recitals, Jazz Cabaret, the outdoor Swing into Summertime concert, music festivals and our annual musical theatre production. Informal recitals and large-scale concerts alike give students of all levels the chance to build confidence and share their talents with the wider school community. Recent musicals have included Billy Elliot, Footloose and Oliver!.
Students are encouraged to join at any stage of their musical journey, with all Year 7 students auditioned early in the year and invited to participate in ensembles. Students at all levels of experience are welcome, and encouraged, to get involved at any point. The aim is to make every student feel welcome in the Music Department, nurturing a life-long love of music.
Individual Music Lessons
Students may opt for individual instrumental or vocal tuition with one of our expert visiting teachers. Lessons are offered on all orchestral instruments, as well as piano, organ, voice, guitar (classical, electric, and bass) and drums.
Students are regularly entered for Associated Board Music Exams and other recognised qualifications, with many achieving distinctions at the highest levels.
LAMDA & Trinity Musical Theatre
In addition to instrumental and vocal lessons, students can pursue LAMDA (London Academy of Music & Dramatic Art) qualifications and Trinity Musical Theatre exams, developing acting, singing and performance skills. These programmes provide structured learning, performance opportunities, and nationally recognised assessments, helping students grow in confidence and artistic excellence.
Whether performing at an evening concert, participating in graded examinations, or rehearsing at lunchtime, students at Reading Blue Coat are encouraged to explore, enjoy, and excel in their musical and performance journey.
Public Speaking
The art of public speaking and debating is a real strength at Reading Blue Coat, and we are proud of the confidence and eloquence our students display. We have developed a strong internal structure to inspire interest, build skills and encourage commitment from students at every stage of their journey.
We view public speaking as a vital life skill, and students begin developing their ability early on. As part of the Activities Programme, all students in Years 7 and 8 take part in an introductory course designed to build their confidence, clarity and presentation technique.
For those wishing to take their speaking further, we offer weekly after-school clubs across the Junior, Middle and Senior Schools, led by experienced and passionate staff. Students regularly host public speaking evenings for parents and act as compères for concerts and school events, building poise in front of a range of audiences.
House competitions in debating and public speaking are a highlight of the co-curricular calendar. These events showcase quick thinking, humour and persuasive communication.

Sport
Sport is at the heart of life at Reading Blue Coat. Our sports programme is led by a dedicated team of experienced professionals who are passionate about developing every student. Drawing on both internal expertise and specialist external coaches, we provide outstanding instruction for all students, from those pursuing top-level competition to those discovering a lifelong enjoyment of sport.
Our sporting ethos is rooted in the school’s core values of aspiration, compassion, courage, integrity, and service. These principles underpin every aspect of our sports provision, from the U12Es through to the first teams. Blue Coat teams consistently achieve success at county, regional, and national level, with many students progressing to university scholarships or professional sporting pathways. Above all, we strive to instil a lifelong love of sport, equipping every student with the skills, confidence, and motivation to sustain their physical and mental wellbeing long after they leave school.
Sport is for All
Sport at Reading Blue Coat is inclusive and accessible to all. Over 80% of pupils regularly represent the school in sporting fixtures, with almost 100 teams competing across 17 different sports. All students in Years 7–9 have a double PE lesson each week, delivered in mixed-ability and mixed-gender classes. The curriculum places a strong emphasis on fundamental movement skills, with a particular focus on health-related fitness, swimming, and gymnastics.
In addition, every student benefits from a timetabled triple-period Games afternoon each week. In the younger year groups, the programme is centred around our focus sports, while older students enjoy an increasingly broad range of sporting options. This core provision is further enhanced by an extensive co-curricular programme of clubs and recreational activities, ensuring that every student can find enjoyment, challenge, and fulfilment through sport.

Our Sports
We offer three distinct strands of sport at Reading Blue Coat, ensuring opportunities for all students, regardless of ability or ambition.
Focus Sports
This programme is designed to promote maximum participation within our focus sports. After-school training sessions support weekly Games afternoons, with the majority of competitive fixtures taking place on Saturdays.
Athletics
Athletics is an outstanding summer sport in its own right, while also playing a vital role in developing speed, strength, and power that enhances performance across a wide range of other sports. Our major competition is the English Schools Track & Field Cup, where Reading Blue Coat teams regularly qualify for the South West Regional A Final.
In addition, we field District and Town Championship teams, with Reading Blue Coat students frequently forming a significant part of the Reading District Team that competes at the County Championships. In recent years, several Blue Coat athletes have progressed to the English Schools Championships, the most prestigious competition for school athletes nationally.
Cricket
Cricket continues to thrive in popularity among both boys and girls. In recent years, the programme has grown significantly, with our cricket club competing on a demanding and prestigious fixture circuit. Regular opponents include leading cricket schools such as Abingdon, Bradfield, RGS Guildford, Portsmouth Grammar, Radley, Wellington College, and the renowned MCC.
The majority of fixtures are played on Saturday, complemented by additional midweek matches. Teams across all age groups up to U15 compete in the County Cup, while the 1st XI represents the school in the esteemed HMC National T20 competition. As part of our annual Cricket Week, we also host our own T20 Festival, which continues to grow in both reputation and reach.
Reading Blue Coat is proud to be the home of the Berkshire Youth Cricket Training Centre, serving as a hub for county age-group training and fixtures. This close partnership provides a strong player development pathway, and we are delighted that many of our students go on to represent Berkshire, with several progressing further to regional and national honours.
Football
Football is a thriving part of life at Reading Blue Coat and is the focus sport for the boys during the Spring Term. It enjoys the largest participation level across all year groups. At junior level, all boys play football as part of their Games programme, ensuring a strong foundation and high levels of engagement. Additional after-school training sessions are available for all pupils who wish to represent the school. While some fixtures are incorporated into Games lessons, the majority are played on Saturdays.
On average, the school fields 18 teams each Saturday and is both a founding and active participant in the Central Independent Schools League. Teams across all age groups compete in their respective County Cup competitions, providing players with regular opportunities to test themselves at a high and competitive level.
Hockey
The girls’ hockey programme continues to go from strength to strength. An increasing number of Saturday fixtures against like-minded independent schools is complemented by a full programme of midweek matches. After-school training sessions are offered across all age groups and focus on the development of core technical skills, with an emphasis on applying these effectively through tactical awareness and game understanding.
Girls compete in both county and national competitions, and those demonstrating significant potential are actively supported and guided towards representative pathway opportunities.
Netball
Throughout the year, the girls’ Reading Blue Coat Netball Club competes in elite school competitions as well as regional and national tournaments, alongside a full programme of Saturday fixtures. Our teams consistently perform well, and students are able to participate at an appropriate level, from A teams through to D teams, ensuring opportunity and challenge for all.
Players benefit from high-quality coaching that develops both the technical and tactical aspects of the game. This includes positional specialisation sessions, strength and conditioning, and game analysis. Training sessions are high-intensity, goal‑oriented, and carefully tailored to bring out the best in every student.
Rowing
Reading Blue Coat is uniquely placed for rowing, with a beautiful stretch of the River Thames beside the school and an on-site Boathouse near Sonning Lock. Our Rowing Club is thriving and continues to grow, welcoming both boys and girls who train regularly and represent the school in competitions at both local and national level.
From Year 9, rowing becomes available across all three terms. Students train during Games sessions and have access to up to two after-school sessions and Saturday morning outings. They begin structured land training, including ergometer work and circuits, building technical ability and fitness in preparation for national competition.
In Year 10, students transition to sweep rowing (one oar), continuing with weekly games sessions, three after-school practices and Saturday training. This is a key competitive year, with students racing at both local and national events and joining the squad for the annual Easter training camp.
Senior Rowing (Years 11–13)
The senior squad represents the pinnacle of rowing at Reading Blue Coat, with students training intensively and competing in major regattas throughout the UK. Training is demanding, with early starts, multiple weekly sessions and high expectations, but hugely rewarding.
This video captures our crew’s performance in the Princess Elizabeth Challenge Cup at Henley Royal Regatta 2025.
First VIII at Henley Regatta
Rugby
Rugby is the focus sport for boys during the Autumn Term, offering a dynamic and inclusive environment in which players of all abilities can develop their skills, teamwork, and sportsmanship. Regularly fielding up to 16 teams on a Saturday, the programme continues to grow, with increasing interest in both Rugby Sevens and touch rugby.
We are proud to host one of the largest U12 and U13 contact rugby festivals in the country, attracting schools from across the UK, alongside popular U15 touch rugby festivals. All eligible year groups compete in the County Cup, which Reading Blue Coat has won on several occasions in recent years.
At national level, our U15 and 1st XV teams compete in the prestigious Continental Tyres National Schools Cup. Recent highlights include the U15s winning the Bowl final at StoneX Stadium and the 1st XV reaching the Vase semi-final, earning the opportunity to play at Sixways Stadium.
Club Sport
Our Club Sport programme provides opportunity for students whose interests extend beyond the focus sports, with training held at lunchtimes or after school. Competitive opportunities include midweek fixtures in county and national cups and leagues. Recent club sports have included swimming, girls’ football, boys’ hockey, tennis, cross country and golf.
Recreational Sports
Recreational sport is primarily delivered through lunchtime practices and allows pupils to enjoy sport purely for enjoyment and wellbeing. These sessions are non-competitive and focus on participation, with current offerings including strength and conditioning, basketball, badminton and tennis.

Complaints procedure
Reading Blue Coat School has long prided itself on the quality of the teaching and pastoral care provided to its students. However, if parents do have a complaint, they can expect it to be treated by the School with care and in accordance with this Complaints Procedure.
The School makes its Complaints Procedure available to all parents of students and of prospective students on the School’s website and will ensure that parents of students and of prospective students who request it are made aware that this document is published or available, of the form in which it is published or available, and of the number of complaints registered under the formal procedure during the preceding School year.
In accordance with paragraph 32(1) of Schedule 1 to the Education (Independent School Standards) Regulation 2014, the School will also make available, on request, to Ofsted, the Department for Education (DfE) or the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), details of this Complaints Procedure and the number of complaints registered under the formal procedure during the preceding School year.

Aldworth Partnership
At Reading Blue Coat, we believe that education extends far beyond the classroom. Inspired by our founder Richard Aldworth’s vision of service and opportunity, the Aldworth Partnership is our commitment to meaningful community engagement – locally, nationally and globally.
The Aldworth Partnership is the umbrella for all our outreach and service initiatives, and it reflects our School’s values of compassion, leadership and social responsibility. Through this programme, students are encouraged to serve, fundraise and donate in ways that are both impactful and personally enriching.
A Culture of Service
We place great emphasis on service being transformational, not just transactional. Our students don’t simply give – they connect, collaborate and grow through the relationships they build.
Whether mentoring younger children, supporting local charities or leading fundraising campaigns, students develop empathy, initiative and a deep understanding of the world beyond school.
Opportunities to Serve
Service opportunities are embedded throughout school life and open to all students. These include volunteering with local charities, running academic, sporting and creative sessions for nearby primary and secondary schools and supporting community events.
In-school initiatives such as harvest festival food bank donations, Christmas gift and Easter Egg collections and the redistribution of second-hand sports equipment are just a few examples of how students make a tangible difference.
Our Sixth Form students also lead weekly outreach sessions at local schools including Thameside, Rivermead, Highwood, Willow Bank. These partnerships are built on trust, continuity and shared purpose.
A Student-Led Partnership
The Aldworth Partnership is proudly student-led. Our prefects and Service Ambassadors play a central role in shaping the programme – choosing partner charities, organising events and inspiring their peers to get involved.
This leadership experience is both empowering and purposeful, helping students to leave a legacy of service for future generations of Blue Coat students.
To explore our current outreach work and case studies, visit our page on the Schools Together website.
A Global Perspective
The Aldworth Partnership, working in collaboration with our Adventure Education initiative, extends its impact far beyond our local community. Recently, students have taken part in life‑changing overseas projects in Eswatini. Our students have made an inspiring start to their community work here, supporting the Posela Neighbourhood Care Point – a vital hub offering local children nourishment, education and care. Their efforts have already made a meaningful impact: constructing new facilities supported by funds raised at the Christmas Fair (£1,000 to furnish a classroom), preparing vegetable gardens, painting the roof and building a new pit latrine. Throughout the project, they have demonstrated exceptional teamwork, dedication and a genuine commitment to helping the community thrive. These experiences require commitment, planning and fundraising – and offer unforgettable lessons in global citizenship.
A Lasting Impact
We are proud that every student at Reading Blue Coat can serve in a meaningful and uplifting way during their time with us. Research shows that those who serve are more likely to lead fulfilled, connected lives – and we see that truth reflected in our students every day.
The Aldworth Partnership is not just about giving back. It’s about growing together. Through meaningful service in the community, both at home and abroad, our students discover the power of compassion, collaboration and shared purpose. These experiences shape confident, globally minded young people who understand that real change happens when we learn, serve and grow side by side.

Leadership Team and Governors
At Reading Blue Coat, our teaching and operations staff form a dedicated, highly qualified team, united by a shared purpose: to provide the best possible education and pastoral care for every student.
The strength of our School lies not only in the expertise of our staff, but in the collaborative, supportive environment they create. Visitors and parents frequently comment on the warm, respectful relationships between staff and students – a distinctive hallmark of life at Blue Coat.
Leadership is provided by the Head and the Senior Leadership Team, who oversee the day-to-day running of the School and drive strategic development.
Our Governors play an essential role in ensuring the School remains forward-thinking, well governed and true to its values.
Click below to meet members of our Senior Leadership Team and Board of Governors.
Meet our team
Mr Peter Thomas
A move into teaching began at The Judd School in Tonbridge, where he taught for two years, before joining Dauntsey’s School Geography Department. Peter was Housemaster of both Day and Boarding Houses and, amongst other things, enjoyed coaching football and rugby and running the Christian Union.
Mr Peter Thomas
Pete joined Reading Blue Coat in September 2015 as Second Master and took over as Headmaster in September 2020.
Born and raised in Horsham, West Sussex, Peter enjoyed sport and read Geology at Durham University, before working for five years as a Response Officer for Sussex Police. A move into teaching began at The Judd School in Tonbridge, where he taught for two years, before joining Dauntsey’s School Geography Department. Peter was Housemaster of both Day and Boarding Houses and, amongst other things, enjoyed coaching football and rugby and running the Christian Union.
Peter and his wife Emily, a language teacher, are parents to four sons, and their mostly obedient Labrador, Arthur. ‘Down time’ means time as a family, perhaps enjoying some camping, being involved with a church and enjoying the delights of the Blue Coat area.

Mrs Alexandra West
Alexandra joined Reading Blue Coat in April 2024 form her role as Bursar of Magdalen College School, Oxford. Prior to this she was the Deputy Bursar here at Blue Coat before her appointment at MCS in 2020.
Previously, Alexandra served as an Intelligence Officer in the British Army and also worked as an equity research analyst in the City. Alexandra brings to Blue Coat tremendous financial acumen, wisdom, humour and a track record of moulding teams to successfully tackle all situations.
Alexandra earned a first-class degree in Music from New College, Oxford University as well as gaining a Full Blue (rowing). Married to Neal and with two children, she is a keen cyclist, rower and skier.

Mrs Sarah Bunnell-Pyper

Prior to this, Sarah worked at St Peter’s College, Oxford and at Greene’s Tutorial College, Oxford. She holds a BA (Hons) in Performing Arts, Communication, Media and Culture from Oxford Brookes University. Sarah was instrumental in setting up the Foundation Office at Reading Blue Coat which has sought to formalise engagement with the wider Blue Coat community. This included curating the Old Blues events programme, editing the first edition of our alumni magazine, 1646 and setting up our community engagement platform, Reading Blue Coat Connect. Sarah has also overseen fundraising projects at the School such as the ‘Defined by Vision, United by Ambition’ Foundation Award campaign and the fundraising for the Performing Arts Centre.
Sarah is a true lover of the performing arts, particularly theatre having performed onstage throughout her life. In her spare time she likes to go to the theatre, read novels, go walking by the river or spend time in Scotland where she grew up. Mostly, though she enjoys spending time with her husband Tom and their daughter Josephina.

Charlie joined Reading Blue Coat in December 2024 from Magdalen College School, where he was Director of Marketing and Communications.
Before moving to Oxford, Charlie spent seven years at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, in various roles including Head of External Relations and Bye Fellow. Charlie started his career in the financial services sector and retains a keen interest in business and global affairs.
Charlie holds a prize-winning first-class degree in Geography from the University of Liverpool and an MPhil in Latin American Studies from the University of Cambridge, where he was awarded a Simón Bolívar Scholarship. Outside of work, he is a governor of a local primary school and enjoys football, cycling and hiking.

Welcome to Reading Blue Coat
Founded in 1646, Reading Blue Coat is a school rich in heritage, yet firmly focused on the future. Underpinned by our values of aspiration, compassion, courage, integrity and service, we aim for excellence in all that we do, for everyone. We want our whole community to thrive: engaged in purpose, and kind in approach.
We are fortunate to enjoy a beautiful 46-acre site fronting the Thames, offering an inspiring setting for stretching both body and mind. From the moment I first walked through the gates and up the drive, I was struck by the thought: what a fabulous place to be at school. Our outstanding outdoor facilities provide space not only for sport and recreation, but for passions to be ignited, skills sharpened and friendships forged – where challenge is met and triumph shared.
Adventures here are not confined to the playing fields. In the classroom, subject experts help to unlock the potential in every pupil, nurturing a love of learning and developing flexible, independent thinkers. We want our students to have the confidence to push doors – or blaze their own trails – and the skills and strength of character to meet whatever lies ahead. Our results reflect that ethos: in 2024-25, 82% of GCSE entries were graded 9-7, and 84% of A Level results were A*-B, opening up wide horizons for our leavers.
Richard Aldworth founded the School more than 360 years ago with a vision to widen access to education. We remain true to that founding purpose through the Aldworth Partnership, a school-wide programme of service, and through bursaries that enable young people of talent and promise to flourish here – contributing richly to our community and gaining greatly in return.
Life at Reading Blue Coat
Looking ahead, we are excited to have extended our long-standing co-educational Sixth Form into Year 7, and we look forward to becoming fully co-educational across all year groups by 2027. The diversity of thought, experience and talent this brings will only enrich an already vibrant school environment.
Visitors often remark on the distinctive character and atmosphere of Blue Coat – a hidden gem in this bucolic corner of Berkshire. I felt exactly the same when I first visited, and my appreciation of this extraordinary place has only deepened since. If you are considering where your son or daughter might thrive – stretched, encouraged and truly known – I warmly invite you to come and see us.
I look forward to meeting you.
Pete Thomas Headmaster
Subject leaders have extensive subject knowledge which they use to plan learning carefully, considering pupils' needs and interests. Their enthusiasm for their subjects inspire pupils to learn creatively and to achieve.

Adventure Education
At Reading Blue Coat, we believe that some of the most valuable learning takes place beyond the classroom. Our Adventure Education programme is a central part of our commitment to developing well-rounded, confident, and resilient young people.
Adventure Education is closely linked with our whole-school Activities Programme, which runs weekly for every year group. The department leads a wide range of exciting pursuits that challenge and inspire. Students are encouraged to challenge themselves physically and mentally, build character, and forge lasting connections with others. Activities such as climbing, paddleboarding, mountain biking, bushcraft, and team challenges promote self-reliance, problem-solving, and leadership — all within fun, dynamic, and supportive environments.
At the heart of our provision are the Combined Cadet Force (CCF) and the Duke of Edinburgh’s Award (DofE). These nationally recognised programmes provide structured opportunities for students to develop responsibility, discipline, and teamwork. Whether through drills and fieldcraft in the CCF, or volunteering, skills, physical challenges, and expeditions in DofE, these experiences lay the foundation for personal growth that extends well beyond school life.
Adventure Education Facilities
At Reading Blue Coat School, we have developed a diverse range of outdoor adventure facilities designed to encourage students to challenge themselves both physically and mentally, while building resilience and character.
Our unique riverside location is fully utilised, offering activities such as raft building and paddleboarding. Along the wooded riverbank, students can explore our dedicated bushcraft camp, as well as a mountain biking course that winds up and down the natural slopes. In addition, we are proud to offer an extensive low- and high-ropes course, providing opportunities for climbing, teamwork, and problem-solving.
All of these facilities have been purposefully created to provide meaningful challenges that promote self-reliance, leadership, and collaborative skills, all within a fun, dynamic, and supportive environment.
Combined Cadet Force (CCF)
The Combined Cadet Force is one of many enriching opportunities available to students in Year 9 and above, offering those who take part the chance to build confidence, character and leadership skills in a dynamic and supportive environment.
The CCF is a voluntary youth organisation that encourages resilience, initiative, teamwork, self-discipline and courage. Our contingent is one of the most popular co-curricular choices at the School and cadets often find the experience both rewarding and great fun.
Students can join one of three sections: the Royal Navy, the Army, or the Royal Air Force (RAF). Each service promotes leadership and teamwork through its own distinctive set of activities. Cadets might find themselves sailing at Dinton Pastures with the Royal Navy, taking part in live firing exercises with the Army or flying at RAF Benson with the RAF.
The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award (DofE)
The Duke of Edinburgh’s Award (DofE) at Reading Blue Coat is a fantastic programme that encourages independence through challenges in volunteering, physical activity, skill development and adventurous expeditions.
The DofE programme is structured across year groups: Bronze is offered in Year 9, Silver in Year 10, and Gold from Years 11 to 13. Preparation and support for students takes place after school and occasional weekends.
Expeditions provide unforgettable experiences, promoting self-reliance and a love for the outdoors. Our students have explored stunning locations such as the Chilterns and Corfe Castle in Swanage, where they’ve had the chance to develop strong leadership skills, take initiative, and support one another through real-world challenges.
Volunteering is an important part of the DofE journey, encouraging giving back and making a meaningful difference in the wider community.
With a thriving DofE community at Reading Blue Coat, participation is consistently high, and many students complete multiple levels of the award. It’s a fantastic way to enhance a CV, broaden horizons and take pride in meaningful achievements beyond the classroom.
Expeditions
Expeditions are another key feature of the Adventure offering. Each academic year includes opportunities for unforgettable experiences – this summer, our students travelled to Eswatini, contributing to the Posela Neighbourhood Care Point – a vital space that provides local children with nourishment, education and care. At the end of the school year, all students take part in residential trips, with destinations including Pembrokeshire, Devon and the Peak District.

Performing Arts
In the Performing Arts, students are encouraged to take creative risks, work with passion and discipline, and express themselves with confidence, all within a supportive and dynamic community.
At Reading Blue Coat, the Performing Arts are far more than a co-curricular offering – they are a vital part of how students learn, grow and connect with the world around them.
The purpose of all art is, ultimately, to explore the meaning and purpose of existence. In the Performing Arts, we discover new ways of seeing – new ways of understanding ourselves, others and our place in the wider world. Artistic expression demands more than talent: it calls for imagination, courage, discipline and openness. It invites students to let go of preconceptions, embrace creativity and allow space for transformation – of ideas, of perspective and often, of self.
Students engage with a broad range of artistic disciplines including Dance, Drama, Music, Public Speaking and Technical Theatre, as well as the visual arts such as painting and sculpture. Across all these fields, their achievements are frequently outstanding and recognised at local, national and international levels.
Our vibrant calendar of concerts, recitals, productions, exhibitions and debates is a highlight of school life. These events are not only a celebration of student talent, but also of community spirit, and we are always delighted to welcome parents, friends and alumni to support and share in these moments.
Whether on stage, behind the scenes or at the podium, every student is given the chance to find their voice and pursue excellence. With opportunities to perform in professional-standard productions, compete on international stages or simply explore the joy of creative expression, the Performing Arts are a vibrant and integral part of life at Reading Blue Coat.
Drama
The Drama Department at Reading Blue Coat is a vibrant and dynamic space where stories are brought to life. Through performance, design and critical exploration, students are encouraged to think creatively, collaborate with others, and develop their voice. Whether working on a script, devising original work or taking to the stage, students build confidence, empathy, and a deeper understanding of the world around them.
Dance
The Dance Department at Reading Blue Coat is an energetic and expressive environment where students develop technique, strength, and artistry. Through a range of styles and performance opportunities, students are challenged to push their physical boundaries while exploring creativity through movement. Dance at RBC fosters discipline, resilience and a strong sense of ensemble, empowering students to perform with confidence and individuality.
Curricular Drama
All students in Year 7 enjoy dedicated Drama lessons, where they are introduced to key theatrical terminology and the foundations of theatre history. In Years 8 & 9, students can choose Drama, allowing them to further develop their skills through the exploration of a range of genres and texts, alongside practical experience in elements such as lighting and sound design.
At GCSE and A Level, students follow the Eduqas specification. Students can specialise in acting or technical/design pathways, developing their understanding of influential practitioners such as Augusto Boal, Bertolt Brecht and Konstantin Stanislavski. Through both scripted and devised work, they grow as performers, directors, designers, and thoughtful critics.
Learning is enriched through a wide range of opportunities beyond the classroom. Theatre Maker Days provide students with the chance to experience professional performance in a variety of settings – from West End productions to more intimate venues such as The Mill at Sonning – broadening their understanding of style, genre, and theatrical practice.
Curricular Dance
Dance was introduced into the curriculum in September 2023 under the leadership of our Head of Dance, marking an exciting and ambitious development in the Performing Arts provision at Reading Blue Coat.
The Dance curriculum is designed to develop students’ technical ability, physical confidence, and creative expression. From the outset, all students in Year 7 have Dance lessons and students are encouraged to explore a range of styles and techniques, building strength, coordination, and performance quality. Alongside this, they begin to develop their choreographic voice, learning how to create and communicate meaning through movement.
As the subject continues to grow, students will have the opportunity to pursue Dance at GCSE and A Level. At GCSE, students develop their skills as both performers and choreographers, studying set works and analysing professional repertoire alongside practical performance and composition. At A Level, this is extended further, with a deeper focus on technical excellence, choreographic intention and critical appreciation of key practitioners and dance styles.
Across all key stages, students are encouraged to think creatively, work collaboratively, and refine their physical and expressive skills. The curriculum fosters discipline, resilience, and artistry, supporting students to grow not only as dancers, but as confident and reflective performers.
Learning is enhanced through performance opportunities and exposure to live and recorded professional work, enabling students to engage with dance as both an art form and a means of communication.
Co-Curricular Drama
Performance is at the heart of the Drama co-curricular programme, with a variety of productions staged throughout the year:
Students are encouraged to take on a variety of roles, from acting and directing to technical and design work, helping them develop confidence, creativity, and collaboration skills.
Co-Curricular Dance
Dance is a dynamic and vibrant part of our co-curricular programme. Students can take part in a wide range of classes and styles, including contemporary, street, commercial, ballet and jazz.
The annual Dance Show is a highlight of the year, showcasing the creativity, athleticism, and dedication of our dancers. Blue Coat also competes in inter-school competitions, giving students the opportunity to perform at a high-level while being part of a supportive and exciting performance community.
Through both performance and competition, students develop technique, artistry, and confidence, while enjoying the collaborative and expressive nature of dance.
Technical Theatre
Every production is supported by a student technical crew, who gain hands-on experience in lighting, sound and set design under the expert guidance of our Theatre Technical Director. We maintain the highest standards in health and safety across our performance spaces.
For those wanting to get involved with technology in the arts, the School Media Team meet as a weekly Technical Theatre club.
Music
The aim of the Music Department is to provide a wealth of opportunities for all students to make and enjoy music. Whether it’s singing in choirs, composing film soundtracks, listening to music from a range of cultures or recording songs in our studio, music at RBC is for everyone.
Music is taught both as an academic subject and through an extensive co-curricular programme. In the classroom, students are encouraged to explore composition, performance and music appreciation. Beyond lessons, we offer a vibrant array of ensembles including our Jazz Band, Rock Bands, String Orchestra, Choirs and smaller wind and brass groups. Theory and composition clubs further extend our provision.
Curricular Music
Music lessons are designed to develop the interconnected skills of listening, performing, composing and appraising. Studying music enables students to become creative thinkers, analytical problem solvers, and effective communicators.
Throughout Key Stage 3 Music, students:
• Build core listening, composing and performing skills. • Acquire musical vocabulary and develop the necessary skills to apply it effectively. • Develop their ability to describe and evaluate music, forming views and expressing and justifying personal opinions. • Strengthen their musical ear and notational awareness. • Understand different musical traditions and the role music plays in both our national identity and global culture, as well as in personal identity. • Explore how ideas, experiences and emotions are conveyed in music from different times and cultures. • Understand the potential of music technology and develop skills in using it to create their own music.
GCSE Music is a popular subject in which students can develop their own musical interests as well as their skills. Students have achieved excellent results, and we follow the OCR specification.
A Level Music is ideal for passionate musicians who want to delve into musical analysis and compose and perform at a high level. Results have been superb, and many students go on to study music at university or conservatoire.
Co-Curricular Music
Whether students take individual lessons or not, there is a broad co-curricular programme. The programme includes:
• Symphony Orchestra (for all instrumentalists) • Big Band (for advanced players) • Bash Cats (the junior jazz band) • Chamber Choir (by audition) • Treble Choir (for Years 7 and 8) • Senior String Ensemble (for advanced players) • Rock bands, alongside several smaller wind and brass groups • Theory and composition sessions
All students in Year 7 are auditioned and invited to join ensembles. However, students are welcome and encouraged to join at any point in their musical journey.
We aim to provide a wide range of performance opportunities for students at all stages of their development. Large formal concerts, showcasing ensembles and soloists, are a wonderful celebration. Equally, smaller informal recitals provide valuable opportunities for students to build confidence.
Individual Music Lessons, LAMDA & Trinity Musical Theatre
Students at Reading Blue Coat have the opportunity to develop their musical and performance skills through a range of individual tuition and graded performance programmes.
Inspiring Events
Across the academic year, our young musicians – supported by a talented team of staff – take part in an inspiring calendar of events, including the Grand Concert, chamber concerts and recitals, Jazz Cabaret, the outdoor Swing into Summertime concert, music festivals and our annual musical theatre production. Informal recitals and large-scale concerts alike give students of all levels the chance to build confidence and share their talents with the wider school community. Recent musicals have included Billy Elliot, Footloose and Oliver!.
Students are encouraged to join at any stage of their musical journey, with all Year 7 students auditioned early in the year and invited to participate in ensembles. Students at all levels of experience are welcome, and encouraged, to get involved at any point. The aim is to make every student feel welcome in the Music Department, nurturing a life-long love of music.
Individual Music Lessons
Students may opt for individual instrumental or vocal tuition with one of our expert visiting teachers. Lessons are offered on all orchestral instruments, as well as piano, organ, voice, guitar (classical, electric, and bass) and drums.
Students are regularly entered for Associated Board Music Exams and other recognised qualifications, with many achieving distinctions at the highest levels.
LAMDA & Trinity Musical Theatre
In addition to instrumental and vocal lessons, students can pursue LAMDA (London Academy of Music & Dramatic Art) qualifications and Trinity Musical Theatre exams, developing acting, singing and performance skills. These programmes provide structured learning, performance opportunities, and nationally recognised assessments, helping students grow in confidence and artistic excellence.
Whether performing at an evening concert, participating in graded examinations, or rehearsing at lunchtime, students at Reading Blue Coat are encouraged to explore, enjoy, and excel in their musical and performance journey.
Public Speaking
The art of public speaking and debating is a real strength at Reading Blue Coat, and we are proud of the confidence and eloquence our students display. We have developed a strong internal structure to inspire interest, build skills and encourage commitment from students at every stage of their journey.
We view public speaking as a vital life skill, and students begin developing their ability early on. As part of the Activities Programme, all students in Years 7 and 8 take part in an introductory course designed to build their confidence, clarity and presentation technique.
For those wishing to take their speaking further, we offer weekly after-school clubs across the Junior, Middle and Senior Schools, led by experienced and passionate staff. Students regularly host public speaking evenings for parents and act as compères for concerts and school events, building poise in front of a range of audiences.
House competitions in debating and public speaking are a highlight of the co-curricular calendar. These events showcase quick thinking, humour and persuasive communication.

Our History
Richard Aldworth
Reading Blue Coat was founded in 1646 by Richard Aldworth, a London merchant and Governor of Christ’s Hospital. His vision was to provide “education and bringing upp of twenty poore male children” in Reading, and so began the story of a school rooted in charity, character and community.
Originally known as Aldworth’s Hospital, the School was first located near St Mary’s Minster Church in Reading. The boys wore the distinctive blue coat and cap, a tradition that lives on today in the ceremonial dress worn by senior prefects.
A Journey Through Time
Over the centuries, Reading Blue Coat has evolved in response to the changing needs of society. From the introduction of science and art in the 19th century to the admission of day boys and the establishment of a Sixth Form, the School has continually expanded its academic and pastoral provision.
Milestones of Progress
1987: The Sixth Form became fully co-educational.
A Legacy of Giving
The School’s history is shaped not only by its founders but also by generous benefactors such as John West and Ann Norwood, whose contributions helped sustain and expand the School’s charitable mission. Their names now live on in two of our Houses, reinstated in 2021 to honour their legacy.
Truth Conquers All
Our motto, Veritas Omnia Vincit – Truth Conquers All –captures the enduring spirit of Reading Blue Coat. It reflects the School’s commitment to integrity, resilience and excellence across generations.
From its charitable origins to its modern-day reputation for academic and co-curricular strength, Reading Blue Coat continues to build on its proud heritage while preparing students to shape the future.

Futures
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) is embedded throughout the curriculum at Reading Blue Coat, meeting the eight benchmarks of Good Career Guidance set out by Gatsby.
During Years 7–11, students study the world of work as part of our PSHE provision, including lessons on career choices, the labour market, employment, employment rights and CV writing.
In Year 10, students undertake Morrisby Assessments, which generate a detailed 20-page report highlighting each individual’s strengths, suggested A Level subject choices and potential career paths. This report is then used in Year 11 by tutors to support students as they decide on their Sixth Form subjects.
In the Sixth Form, Year 12 students benefit from a timetabled Futures lesson that follows a diverse and engaging curriculum, helping them to explore a broad range of future options. Year 13 students receive individual support through regular conversations with their tutors and other appropriate staff (e.g. the Assistant Director of Sixth Form).
All students have regular one-to-one meetings with their tutors, access to Morrisby and Unifrog and benefit from a weekly Futures newsletter sent to the whole school community. They also participate in trips, Futures lunches, and reflective sessions that focus on identifying and developing their transferable skills (DELTAs).
RBC Futures Timeline
Year 7: Life Beyond School – Careers and Your Future (PSHE)
Delivered through PSHE, students begin exploring the concept of careers, personal aspirations and what life beyond school might look like.
Year 8: Life Beyond School – Labour Market Information and Exploring Careers (PSHE)
Students learn how the workplace operates and begin to identify how their skills and interests might align with different sectors.
Year 9: Life Beyond School – Employment and Financial Management (PSHE)
This module introduces the fundamentals of employment and personal finance, including budgeting and managing money.
Year 10: Life Beyond School – Employment Rights and Understanding a Payslip (PSHE)
Students learn about their rights at work, workplace expectations and how to interpret a payslip. They also complete the Morrisby Assessments in the Summer Term, which provide valuable insights into strengths, subject options and future career pathways.
Year 11: Life Beyond School – Writing a CV and Personal Statement (PSHE)
Students are guided in writing their first CV and personal statement, key skills for both Sixth Form applications and future opportunities. Their Morrisby Report is used to inform subject choices for the Sixth Form.
Year 12: Futures and Next Steps
Students begin the UCAS process through a dedicated weekly Futures lesson, meeting the eight Gatsby Benchmarks and preparing for university, apprenticeships, and other post-18 routes.
Year 13: Final Steps
Students complete their UCAS applications and receive tailored support regarding gap years, apprenticeships and alternative pathways, ensuring they are equipped to make confident and informed decisions.
Tutor Meetings
As part of their regular one-to-one meetings with tutors, students receive tailored advice and guidance at key moments in their academic journey – for example, when making decisions about GCSEs, A Levels and university or post-18 options.
To ensure students are future-ready and equipped to navigate an ever-evolving job market, tutors incorporate the McKinsey & Company Distinct Elements of Talent (DELTAs) framework into these discussions. This reflective exercise helps students identify their transferable skills and recognise the broad range of attributes they are developing through their engagement in our exceptional co-curricular programme. It also supports them in building greater self-awareness and confidence in their future planning.
Trips & Events
At Reading Blue Coat, we believe that real-world exposure is key to helping students make informed choices about their futures. Our Futures programme incorporates a wide variety of events and opportunities that connect students with industry professionals, universities and alumni.
Futures Lunches
Throughout the academic year, we welcome Old Blues, parents and local businesses to deliver informal lunchtime talks. These sessions enrich our curriculum with practical careers-focused information, advice and guidance.
Futures Trips
Year 10 students enjoy an annual visit to a workplace with a Careers in STEM focus — recent examples include a behind-the-scenes tour of Silverstone Circuit. Students also attend relevant external events, such as the Henley Female Network meetings at Leander Club, to gain insights into different sectors and career paths.
Morrisby Testing
In Year 10, all students complete a series of Morrisby assessments. These generate a comprehensive, personalised report identifying individual strengths, A Level subject recommendations and possible future careers. In Year 11, this report is used as a foundation for discussions with tutors to guide subject choices. A dedicated parent feedback evening is also held to explain the results and next steps.
Futures Convention
Held in the Summer Term and open to students in Years 11 and 12, our annual Futures Convention brings together a wide range of universities and employers – including Oxbridge and Russell Group institutions – to showcase both degree courses and degree-level apprenticeship opportunities. Students from local partner schools are also invited to attend.
Higher Education Evening
Taking place around Easter, this event is open to all Year 12 students and provides targeted guidance on the university application process. We are joined by expert advisors from Russell Group university admissions teams, such as the University of Birmingham.
Futures Days
During Activities Week, Year 12 students participate in dedicated Futures Days, where they receive expert advice on writing personal statements, understanding student finances and preparing for university life. Additional sessions include careers talks from Old Blues and parents, organised in partnership with our Foundation Office.

Results and Destinations
Academic outcomes at Reading Blue Coat are consistently excellent, with the last three years of A Level results among the strongest in the School’s history.
In 2026, 51% of all A Level grades were A*–A. Five students earned a full set of A*s. At a time of significant change in the educational landscape – with linear exams and evolving syllabuses – we are proud that our students continue to excel in the Sixth Form.
Strong results are just one part of the story. The destinations of our leavers also reflect their ambition and achievement: over 85% of students secured a place at their first-choice university. In 2024, six students took up places at Oxford and Cambridge, while others progressed to leading universities including Bath, Bristol, Durham, Exeter, King’s College London, Imperial College London and Nottingham.
GCSE Results
GCSE results at Reading Blue Coat have remained consistently high over the past five years, reflecting the strength of teaching and the commitment of our students. In 2026, 80% of GCSE grades were 7 or higher, with 57% at grades 8 or 9. We are delighted that our students continue to perform so well and lay such strong academic foundations for future success.

At Reading Blue Coat, we are proud to continue the legacy of our founder, Richard Aldworth, whose vision was to make education accessible to those who might not otherwise have the opportunity.
Rooted in our history and ethos, Foundation Awards reflect our enduring commitment to community, service and educational excellence. Each year, we offer up to two Foundation Awards to new students. These awards are means-tested and cover 100% of tuition fees, along with additional costs such as lunches, transport, uniform, equipment and trips. By removing financial barriers, we ensure that exceptional young people can thrive within our vibrant, inclusive school community.
Who We Are Looking For

A Coaching Culture
At Reading Blue Coat, we believe that education is not just about knowledge – it’s about growth, reflection and unlocking potential. That’s why we’ve embraced a coaching culture across our School community, empowering students and staff alike to develop greater self-awareness, confidence and resilience.
Empowering Conversations
Coaching at Blue Coat is built on meaningful conversations. Whether between students and tutors, staff and colleagues, or peers supporting one another, coaching encourages active listening, thoughtful questioning and reflective thinking. It’s a way of working that fosters trust, curiosity and personal responsibility.
Developing Leadership and Character
Our coaching approach plays a central role in developing leadership and character. Students are supported to set goals, reflect on their progress and take ownership of their learning journey. Sixth Formers, prefects and peer mentors are trained to use coaching techniques to guide and support younger pupils, building a culture of encouragement and mutual respect.
Coaching for Staff
Staff at Blue Coat also benefit from coaching as part of their professional development. Through structured programmes and informal peer support, teachers and support staff are encouraged to reflect on their practice, share ideas and grow together. This culture of openness and collaboration strengthens our whole community.
A Culture That Lasts
Coaching is not a one-off intervention – it’s a mindset. By embedding coaching into the everyday life of the School, we help students and staff build the skills they need to thrive not just at Blue Coat, but in life beyond. It’s a culture that nurtures independence, empathy and lifelong learning.

Equality Diversity and Inclusion
At Reading Blue Coat, we want every student to feel a sense of belonging within the School community and to feel comfortable being themselves. We aim to celebrate individuality and raise awareness and understanding of what makes each of us unique.
Inclusion Groups
We have a range of Inclusion Groups, offering students the opportunity to celebrate aspects of their identity, meet like-minded people and lead meaningful change within the School. Members of our Inclusion Groups lead assemblies, organise events and regularly meet with senior staff to share feedback on issues important to them.
Café Neuro
This student-led group supports and explores matters relating to neurodiversity. Discussions also include broader wellbeing and learning issues, and the group provides a friendly, open space in which students can explore both the challenges and unique strengths they experience at school and beyond. Students do not need a formal diagnosis to attend – just a personal interest in the topic.
Inter-Faith Group
Meeting weekly in the School’s Chaplaincy, students from diverse religious and spiritual backgrounds come together to promote mutual understanding, respect and collaboration. The group offers a platform for open dialogue, allowing participants to share their beliefs and traditions and helps foster empathy and community across faiths.
Mandela Society
The Mandela Society discusses issues related to racial and cultural equality. Its aim is to increase awareness and understanding of race, religion and culture at Reading Blue Coat – with a strong focus on celebration and education.
Pride Society
Meeting weekly, Pride Society offers a safe and supportive space for LGBTQ+ students and their allies to connect and share experiences.
SAFE Society
SAFE stands for Striving Altogether For Equality. The group focuses on gender equality and works with the School to propose and organise initiatives that support a more equal and inclusive environment for all.

In the curriculum
Equality, diversity and inclusion are also embedded in the School’s academic and pastoral curriculum. Departments regularly review their content to ensure that a breadth of voices and experiences are represented.
Our PSHE curriculum explores themes such as celebrating differences, world issues and rights and responsibilities, from Years 7 to 13. Students also attend talks and workshops on a range of important topics – recent sessions have included ‘Healthy Masculinity’ and ‘Anti-Racism’.
